name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation College Scholarship
description: U.S. high school seniors graduating spring 2027 and entering an accredited four-year college in fall 2027; minimum unweighted GPA 3.75, required SAT/ACT/AP/IB test score, and financial need with family income reviewed up to $95,000.
deadlineLabel: November 11, 2026

name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
description: For Black/African American high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and demonstrate academic achievement, leadership, service and financial need. Awards total $40,000 over four years; essays and recommendations are required.
deadlineLabel: December 1, 2026 (recommendation deadline December 15)

name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
description: Need-based awards of up to $25,000 for high school juniors who have overcome adversity and demonstrate leadership, service and academic commitment. Check the sponsor for the next application cycle and detailed eligibility; high school seniors should review its other programs.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for the next junior-year application cycle

name: Scholarships360 $10,000 No-Essay Scholarship
description: Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents across high school, undergraduate, graduate, technical and vocational programs. Rolling monthly entry deadlines; one $10,000 award for the cycle, with finalist interviews.
deadlineLabel: June 30, 2027 (rolling monthly entry deadlines)

name: U.S. Bank Student Scholarship Program
description: Legal U.S. residents age 17+, accepted or enrolled in an eligible undergraduate college or trade/vocational program. Financial education modules required; a sweepstakes rather than a need-based award.
deadlineLabel: October 30, 2026

name: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars Program
description: Thirteen $25,000 awards recognize students for academic success, community service and financial need. Includes a one-year leadership development and mentoring program; review the sponsor application for full eligibility.
deadlineLabel: November 3, 2026

name: Mensa Foundation U.S. Scholarship
description: Enrolled in a degree program at an accredited U.S. institution. Requires an essay of up to 550 words on career goals.
deadlineLabel: November 15, 2026

name: VFW Voice of Democracy Scholarship Contest
description: For eligible students in grades 9–12. Submit an original audio essay on the current patriotic theme with an entry form through a participating local VFW Post. National, state and local awards vary.
deadlineLabel: October 31, 2026, midnight; submit through your participating VFW Post

name: Space to Succeed Scholarship
description: For legal U.S. residents age 18+ attending an accredited U.S. college or university. Submit a 500–800 word essay about community involvement, plus required photos and enrollment documentation; three awards in this cycle.
deadlineLabel: November 30, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Central

name: Financial Goals Scholarship
description: U.S. residents age 18 or older who are planning to enroll or currently enrolled in a college degree program; written response required.
deadlineLabel: Monthly — confirm current entry period

name: Union Plus Scholarship
description: For eligible current or retired participating-union members, spouses and dependent children. Applicants must meet membership and enrollment rules; essays weigh heavily in selection. Awards are one-time, but students may reapply in later years.
deadlineLabel: January 31, 2027 (confirm time in sponsor rules)

name: Truman Scholars Program
description: A graduate-study scholarship for eligible college students committed to public-service careers. Applicants must be nominated by their institution; check campus nomination deadlines before the national deadline.
deadlineLabel: February 2, 2027, 11:59 p.m. in your time zone; campus deadlines may be earlier

name: The Christophers Video Contest
description: College student video contest; original video no longer than five minutes interpreting One Person Can Make a Difference. Sponsor prohibits AI-generated video.
deadlineLabel: January 11, 2027

name: Stossel in the Classroom Video Contest
description: Middle school grades5–8, high school grades9–12, or undergraduate college students residing in the U.S./Canada or with a U.S. military address. Submit a one-to-three-minute video on a current prompt.
deadlineLabel: March 12, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern

name: Debt.com Scholarship for Aggressive Applicants
categoryLabel: No essay required to apply broadly
description: Apply to as many scholarships as possible (winning isn't required) and submit proof plus a short statement about the experience.
deadlineLabel: April 1, 2027 (annual)

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
description: Achievement-based awards recognizing leadership and service among eligible students in their final year of high school. The program selects 150 students for $20,000 awards; current citizenship/residency, GPA and school requirements apply.
deadlineLabel: 2027 application is closed; check sponsor for next cycle

name: The Gates Scholarship
description: A highly selective, last-dollar scholarship for outstanding high school seniors from low-income households. Check the official application for current eligibility, funding coverage, required materials and deadlines.
deadlineLabel: 2027-cycle deadline was September 15, 2026 (opened July 15, 2026); now closed — check sponsor for next cycle

name: Dell Scholars Program
description: For the 2027 cycle: Texas high school seniors planning to attend an accredited four-year PUBLIC college or university in Texas; participation in an approved college-readiness program in grades11–12, Pell eligibility and GPA2.4+ required.
deadlineLabel: January 12, 2027

name: QuestBridge National College Match
description: Connects high-achieving high school seniors from low-income backgrounds with partner colleges and full four-year Match Scholarships. Review citizenship, academic and financial criteria and the binding Match process before ranking colleges.
deadlineLabel: 2026 Match applicants have been selected as Finalists; check sponsor for next entry cycle

name: Burger King Scholars Program
description: Scholarships for eligible high school seniors, Burger King employees and employee families pursuing postsecondary college or vocational/technical education. Awards and criteria vary by application track; check the administrator for current requirements.
deadlineLabel: December 15, 2026, 11:59 p.m. CT

name: Elks MVS Scholarship
description: Current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens and plan full-time four-year undergraduate study at an accredited U.S. college. Elks membership/relationship not required.
deadlineLabel: November 12, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific

name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
description: LGBTQ+ AND ally students, at least high school seniors, with GPA3.3+ pursuing full-time undergraduate/graduate/professional degrees at accredited U.S. not-for-profit institutions. 100%online degree programs excluded.
deadlineLabel: November 19, 5 p.m. Pacific (fall 2027 funding; confirm cycle)

name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund Scholar Program
description: Merit-selected HSF Scholars receive support services and may receive a cash award based on need and available funding. Hispanic-heritage students must meet citizenship/residency, GPA and full-time enrollment requirements; a Scholar designation does not guarantee a cash award.
deadlineLabel: 2026 application closed; check sponsor for the next cycle

name: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
description: Scholarships for American Indian and Alaska Native students in certificate, undergraduate or graduate programs at tribal colleges and universities or accredited nonprofit schools. One annual application covers multiple opportunities; eligibility and funding vary.
deadlineLabel: Applications open annually February 1; priority review deadline May 31 (late applications still accepted); spring-term deadline January 25

name: UNCF Scholarships
description: UNCF administers a range of scholarships, fellowships and other student opportunities. Each program has its own school, major, eligibility, essay and deadline requirements; use the official opportunities portal to find a match.
deadlineLabel: Varies by individual scholarship

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
description: For students 18 and under who have completed a significant piece of work in science, technology, math, literature, music, philosophy or outside the box categories.
deadlineLabel: Applications close February 17, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Pacific

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
description: Entry begins through qualifying PSAT/NMSQT participation and program requirements. Semifinalists must complete an application including an essay and meet additional requirements to become Finalists; this is not a no-essay scholarship.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current cycle

name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
description: Graduating high school seniors who are U.S. citizens, demonstrate financial need, academic excellence, leadership and community service, and plan an approved four-year college. Transcript, test score, CSS Profile, essays and recommendation required.
deadlineLabel: January 14, 2027

name: Hagan Scholarship
description: A renewable scholarship with funding determined by educational costs and other aid, plus required workshops and student responsibilities. Review the sponsor’s current academic, income, enrollment and work requirements before applying.
deadlineLabel: December 1, 2026 (for the 2027-2028 academic year)

name: Children of Fallen Patriots Foundation Scholarship
description: College and trade-school scholarships, educational assistance and career support for military children who lost a parent in the line of duty. The program is joining Tunnel to Towers and states that scholarship processing continues; contact the sponsor to confirm eligibility and funding.
deadlineLabel: Contact sponsor about enrollment and funding

name: Imagine America Career College Scholarships
description: Tuition discounts/grants at participating career colleges through separate high-school, adult-learner and military programs. Check your chosen school and program requirements; this is tuition assistance at partner schools rather than unrestricted cash.
deadlineLabel: Varies by school and program

name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
amount: Up to $18,000 associate / $36,000 bachelor, plus possible stipends
description: For eligible low-income Dreamer students attending a participating in-state or online Partner College. Current rules include U.S. arrival before age 16 and before November 1, 2021; international students and temporary nonimmigrant statuses are ineligible. Review all immigration, residency, GPA and enrollment criteria directly with the sponsor.
deadlineLabel: Current round is open; sponsor has not posted a fixed National Scholarship deadline on the page reviewed — check thedream.us/scholarships/national-scholarship/

name: AAUW Career Development Grant
description: Women with at least an associate degree pursuing a short-term accredited certificate/training program in a field where women are underrepresented. Not for a bachelor/master/professional degree program.
deadlineLabel: Next cycle January27–March18, 2027 (5p.m. Eastern deadline)

name: Jeannette Rankin National Scholar Grant
amount: Up to $3,000 per year, renewable up to 5 years
description: Unrestricted, nontuition grants for eligible students age 35+ who self-identify and present as women, pursuing technical/vocational education, a first associate degree or first bachelor degree at an accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. Review income and other sponsor criteria.
deadlineLabel: February 12, 2027; application and recommendation deadline

name: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Award
description: Women with financial need providing primary financial support for themselves AND dependents, enrolled or accepted into undergraduate or vocational training; additional country and prior-award restrictions apply.
deadlineLabel: November 15 (annual; confirm current cycle)

name: Taco Bell Foundation Live Más Scholarship
description: For eligible new applicants ages 16–26 pursuing postsecondary education. Submit either a 30-second–2-minute video or a 250–500-word essay about passion, community and impact. No GPA or test-score requirement; financial need is considered for new 2027 applicants.
deadlineLabel: January 5, 2027, 5 p.m. Pacific

name: American Legion Legacy Scholarship
amount: Up to $20,000 for children of fallen / $5,000 for children of disabled veterans
description: Need-based support for eligible children of U.S. servicemembers who died on active duty on or after September 11, 2001, or post-9/11 veterans with a VA combined disability rating of at least 50%. Review documentation and other aid requirements directly with the sponsor.
deadlineLabel: March 24, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET (2027-28 academic year cycle)

name: DAR Pittenger American History Scholarship
description: For a graduating high school senior pursuing an undergraduate degree with at least 24 credit hours in American history or American government. The$2,000 award may be renewed for up to four years under GPA and transcript requirements; see sponsor for details.
deadlineLabel: Check DAR scholarship portal for current cycle

name: National Honor Society Scholarship
description: Active National Honor Society members who are high school seniors demonstrating leadership, service and scholarship, planning to attend college.
deadlineLabel: November 20, 2026, 5 p.m. ET

name: Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year Scholarships
description: Scholarships for participants advancing through Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year recognition. State winners receive $2,500, regional winners $20,000 and the National Youth of the Year $50,000. Ask your Club about participation and its selection process.
deadlineLabel: Contact your Club about its selection timeline

name: Sallie$2,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: For legal residents of the 50 U.S. states, D.C. or U.S. territories age 16+ who meet the specified college-student, high-school-junior/senior or parent eligibility. Monthly sweepstakes; no essay required. Review official rules before entering.
deadlineLabel: Monthly; next deadline November 30, 2026, then December 31, 2026

name: Niche $2,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: A no-essay drawing for eligible high school, college and graduate students or those planning enrollment within 12 months. Entrants age 13–17 require parental consent/supervision; citizenship or valid-visa and other official-rule restrictions apply.
deadlineLabel: Niche runs a rotating series of differently-named/amounted no-essay drawings (e.g., $2,000/$10,000/$25,000/$50,000 versions) with dated URLs rather than one fixed page — search niche.com directly for the current one

name: Unigo $10,000 Scholarship
description: U.S. legal residents age 14 or older; short original written response of 250 words or fewer required.
deadlineLabel: December 31, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific

name: Appily Easy Money Scholarship
description: A monthly no-essay scholarship for eligible U.S. students age 13+ who create a free Appily account and plan postsecondary enrollment. Complete the profile and entry requirements in the official rules; one winner is selected each month.
deadlineLabel: Monthly entry periods

name: DoSomething.org Easy Scholarships
description: For people ages 13–25 living in the U.S. or U.S. citizens abroad who complete an eligible community-service action and report back. No essay, GPA or recommendation requirement; each action has its own location, rules, award and deadline.
deadlineLabel: Varies by eligible action

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
description: Art and writing recognition and scholarship opportunities for eligible teen entrants. Portfolio scholarships for high school seniors submitting six works can reach$12,500; other awards and regional rules differ. Review current grade, age and submission requirements.
deadlineLabel: Varies by region and category

name: YoungArts
description: A national visual, literary and performing arts competition for eligible students in grades 10–12 or ages 15–18, with U.S. citizenship, residency or taxable-income eligibility requirements. Winners receive cash awards and career/mentorship support.
deadlineLabel: Current application closed; next 2028 application opens summer 2027

name: Society of Women Engineers (SWE) Scholarship Program
description: Scholarships for students in eligible engineering, technology and related programs. Undergraduate tracks require an eligible ABET-accredited program; year-of-study, GPA, graduate-major and regional requirements differ. Recommendations are required; check the relevant application.
deadlineLabel: Collegiate/graduate: Dec 1, 2026–Feb 1, 2027; first-year: Feb 8–Mar 31, 2027

name: AICPA Foundation Legacy Scholarships
description: Awards supporting eligible accounting students pursuing CPA careers, with separate Future CPAs, first-generation/public accounting and two-year-transfer opportunities. GPA, citizenship/residency, enrollment and other rules differ; one application can cover eligible Legacy awards.
deadlineLabel: March 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET (application opens December 1)

name: National FFA Scholarships
description: One application covers multiple scholarship opportunities for senior FFA members in high school and FFA alumni in college, pursuing trade certificates, two-year or four-year programs. Individual sponsors set additional eligibility criteria.
deadlineLabel: Applications open November 1, 2026; due January 14, 2027

name: Jeannette Rankin Foundation Tribal Scholar Grant
description: Unrestricted, non-tuition-specific grants for women age 25 or older who are enrolled members of a federally recognized Tribe (verified by a Certificate of Indian Blood or Tribal Identification Card), attending a Tribal College, pursuing technical/vocational education or a first associate or bachelor's degree, and demonstrating financial need. Grants are renewable for up to five years.
deadlineLabel: February 12, 2027 (application and recommendation letters due)

name: Elks National Foundation Legacy Awards
amount: $6,000 total ($1,500 per year for four years)
description: For high school seniors who are a child, grandchild, step-child, step-grandchild, or legal ward of a living Elks member (membership must have begun on or before April 1, 2024, and be dues-paid through March 31, 2027). 400 awards are offered nationally (251 state-allocated, 149 at-large). Standardized test scores are not required for the 2027 contest.
deadlineLabel: February 1, 2027, 11:59 a.m. Pacific

name: American Legion Auxiliary Children of Warriors National President's Scholarship
description: For high school seniors who are a direct descendant (child, grandchild, or great-grandchild) of a veteran who served April 6, 1917–November 11, 1918, or at any time after December 7, 1941. Requires at least 50 documented volunteer hours completed during high school; American Legion Family membership is not required.
deadlineLabel: March 1 each year, 11:59 p.m. Eastern (no extensions)

name: American Legion Auxiliary Non-Traditional Student Scholarship
description: For non-traditional students — those returning to school after an interruption in formal education or beginning postsecondary study later in life — who are either a two-year paid member of The American Legion/Auxiliary/Sons of The American Legion, an honorably discharged veteran, or the spouse of an active-duty servicemember or honorably discharged veteran. For certified trade, professional, technical, or degree programs.
deadlineLabel: March 1 each year, 11:59 p.m. Eastern (no extensions)

name: SHPE ScholarSHPE Scholarship Program
amount: Varies by individual scholarship (SHPE reports $1,000,000+ awarded annually across roughly 245 scholarships)
description: For active Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE) members who are declared STEM majors with at least a 2.5 cumulative GPA, planning full-time enrollment at an accredited two- or four-year U.S. institution (U.S. territories included). Open to incoming high school seniors through graduate/doctoral students; some sponsor-funded awards add citizenship or major-specific requirements. One common ScholarSHPE application covers all SHPE-administered scholarships.
deadlineLabel: Recent cycle opened February 2 and closed February 16 — check sponsor for the current cycle's exact dates

name: NSBE Scholarships
amount: $500–$17,500 per award, depending on the specific sponsored scholarship
description: For registered, paid National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) members — high school seniors through graduate students — pursuing engineering, computer science, mathematics, or a related STEM field, generally with a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA (individual sponsored scholarships may set higher GPA, residency, or major requirements). One application covers more than 100 sponsored scholarships.
deadlineLabel: Fall/Winter GPA-verification and application window runs September 1, 2026 – February 26, 2027 — check sponsor for the exact scholarship-specific deadline

name: ACS Scholars Program
description: For African American/Black, Hispanic/Latino, or American Indian U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents who are high school seniors or college freshmen/sophomores/juniors (seniors may apply for a 5th year), majoring or intending to major in chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, chemical technology, or another chemistry-related science with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Pre-med, nursing, pharmacy, and veterinary students are not eligible (MD/PhD aspirants are).
deadlineLabel: March 1 each year (application opens November 1)

name: Phi Theta Kappa All-USA Academic Team Scholarship
description: For Phi Theta Kappa community-college members pursuing an associate degree: at least 6 semester credit-hours of college-level coursework, 36+ semester credits completed by December, a minimum 3.50 GPA on coursework from the last 5 years, no prior All-USA or Coca-Cola Academic Team nomination, and a disciplinary record free of suspension or probation. For transfer and workforce students; by college nomination only (not a direct individual application).
deadlineLabel: December 1, 2026 (part of PTK's broader scholarship-application group)

name: P.E.O. Program for Continuing Education (PCE)
description: Need-based grants for women in the U.S. and Canada whose education has been interrupted and who are returning to school to complete a degree or certification that will improve employability. Applicants must be sponsored by a local P.E.O. chapter rather than applying directly online; there is no single universal deadline — check with a local chapter for timing.
deadlineLabel: No fixed national deadline — apply through sponsorship by a local P.E.O. chapter

name: Coolidge Scholarship
amount: Full-ride (tuition, room, board, and expenses for four years at any accredited U.S. college or university)
description: A full-ride presidential scholarship from the Calvin Coolidge Presidential Foundation for current high school juniors (current seniors are not eligible). Recipients are notified in late May of their junior year and may attend any accredited American college or university.
deadlineLabel: Applicants apply during junior year — check coolidgescholars.org for the current cycle's exact deadline

name: TMCF Lowe's Gap Scholarship
amount: Up to $5,000 for the academic year (25 scholars)
description: For full-time undergraduates at a Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) member school (public HBCUs and predominantly Black institutions) majoring in business or a STEM field, with a cumulative GPA of 3.00 or higher and demonstrated financial need. U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents only; funds cover verifiable tuition and standard fees.
deadlineLabel: December 1, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET (application opens June 1, 2026)

name: NABA National Scholarship Program
description: For active student members of the National Association of Black Accountants (NABA) enrolled full-time at an accredited U.S. two- or four-year college or university, who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents with strong academic performance. Selection weighs academic achievement, leadership, service, and engagement with NABA's mission.
deadlineLabel: Application window is shorter than in past years; decisions begin on a rolling basis starting Summer 2026 — check nabainc.org/scholarship for the exact closing date

name: Samsung American Legion Scholarship
amount: $10,000 (10 national scholars), $5,000 (10 national runners-up), $1,250 (remaining department finalists)
description: For students who are a direct descendant (child, grandchild, great-grandchild, or legally adopted child) of a U.S. veteran and who participate in their state's American Legion Boys State or Girls State civic-leadership program. Applicants apply through their Boys State/Girls State program; department (state) finalists must reach American Legion National Headquarters by August 1, with national winners announced by mid-October.
deadlineLabel: Set individually by each Boys State/Girls State program; department finalists due to National Headquarters by August 1

name: NIAF Scholarship Program
amount: $2,500–$12,000, depending on the specific scholarship category
description: For National Italian American Foundation (NIAF) members (a student may use a parent's, guardian's, or grandparent's membership) who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents with at least one ancestor who emigrated from Italy, planning full-time enrollment at an accredited U.S. college or university, generally with a GPA of 3.5 or higher (some categories set lower minimums). More than 20 scholarship categories are available, undergraduate through law/medical level.
deadlineLabel: 2027-2028 cycle: applications open December 1, 2026 and are due March 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET

name: NSPE Education Foundation Scholarships
amount: $2,500–$5,000 by individual scholarship (e.g., Steinman Scholarship $5,000 x5, Auxiliary Legacy Scholarship $5,000 x2, Kimel Engineering Scholarship $2,500 x3, Hightower Fellowship $3,000 x2)
description: For undergraduates (generally entering or continuing junior year) in a four-year ABET-accredited engineering program; some named awards are restricted by gender (Auxiliary Legacy, for women) or state residency (Kimel, for Kansas/Missouri residents). Administered by the National Society of Professional Engineers (NSPE) Education Foundation; all awards depend on available foundation funds each cycle.
deadlineLabel: Application process was set to open "early 2026" for that cycle — check apply.nspe.org for current dates

name: National Federation of the Blind Scholarship Program
amount: More than $300,000 in cash and prizes awarded in total across all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico
description: For legally blind applicants (in both eyes) residing in the U.S., D.C., or Puerto Rico, age 18 or older, pursuing or planning to pursue a full-time post-secondary degree at a U.S. institution (a limited number of awards go to part-time students). Requires an interview with the applicant's NFB state affiliate president, and winners must attend the entire NFB National Convention in person, including all scholarship activities.
deadlineLabel: Historically March 31 each year — confirm the current cycle's deadline at scholarships.nfb.org

name: Jack Kent Cooke Undergraduate Transfer Scholarship
amount: Up to $55,000 per year (last-dollar funding, generally up to 3 years)
description: For community college / two-year-institution students with sophomore status as of January 1, 2027 (or graduates since spring 2022) planning to transfer full-time into a bachelor's program in fall 2027. Requires a cumulative GPA of 3.5+, unmet financial need with household income up to $95,000, and no prior attendance at a four-year institution (narrow exceptions apply). U.S. citizenship is not required and there is no age limit. Applications go through the Common App for Transfer.
deadlineLabel: 2027 cycle: applications open August 19, 2026 and close December 9, 2026

name: National Beta Club Scholarship
amount: Top 5 National Awards: $6,000–$20,000; plus five $2,500 awards and 250 $1,000 awards (all non-renewable)
description: For Senior Beta Club members registered with National Beta Headquarters by the application deadline. Semifinalists must complete an additional semifinalist form roughly two months after the initial deadline.
deadlineLabel: Historically January 15 (no extensions) — confirm the current cycle at betaclub.org

name: Hispanic Heritage Youth Awards
amount: Gold/Silver/Bronze one-time innovation grants per category (amount not published; funds can go toward college or a community-service project)
description: For high school seniors (unweighted GPA 3.0+ on a 4.0 scale, or 7.5+ on a 10.0 scale) graduating spring 2027 and planning to enroll at an accredited higher-education institution in 2027-2028. Recognizes leadership and achievement across categories such as STEM, business/entrepreneurship, education, and the arts; selected honorees must attend a virtual regional awards ceremony.
deadlineLabel: November 1, 2026 (current cycle; now closed — check sponsor for next cycle)

name: Tillman Scholars Program
amount: Average $10,000 per academic year (varies by financial need and cost of attendance); up to 60 scholars selected annually
description: For U.S. active-duty service members, veterans (pre- and post-9/11 eras, all branches including National Guard), and current or surviving spouses of service members/veterans, planning full-time enrollment in an accredited U.S. bachelor's, graduate, or professional degree program (certificates, associate degrees, and trade programs don't qualify; children of veterans are not eligible). No minimum GPA to apply, but a 3.0 GPA is required to renew.
deadlineLabel: 2027-2028 cycle: applications open December 3, 2026 — exact closing date not yet posted, check pattillmanfoundation.org/apply

name: Optimist International Essay Contest
amount: $2,500 at the District level (club-level winners advance to District competition)
description: For students under 19 as of October 1 of the contest year who have not yet completed high school or its equivalent (including CEGEP in Québec). Entrants compete first at the local sponsoring Optimist Club level on an annual theme, with club winners advancing to a District contest for a $2,500 college scholarship. Entry is through the District where the student lives (or, for U.S. students on overseas military installations, the District of their last permanent U.S. home).
deadlineLabel: Set by each local sponsoring Optimist Club, typically by early February — contact your local Club for its exact date

name: C-SPAN StudentCam Documentary Competition
amount: $250–$5,000 per student prize (Grand Prize $5,000; First $3,000; Second $1,500; Third $750; Honorable Mention $250), plus matching teacher/school prizes
description: A national documentary competition for students in grades 6-12 (middle school and high school compete in separate divisions) who produce a short documentary responding to C-SPAN's annual civics theme. Prize money is split evenly among all students who produced a winning entry; additional $100 prizes are offered for behind-the-scenes production photos.
deadlineLabel: Entries due by 11:59 p.m. PT, Wednesday, January 20, 2027

name: Bold.org "Be Bold" No-Essay Scholarship
description: Open to all students — high school, undergraduate, or graduate level — regardless of state, field of study, or GPA. No essay is required; the winner is chosen for the "boldest" Bold.org profile, reflecting earnestness, determination, and momentum rather than academic accomplishment alone. Applying earlier in the cycle improves the odds of winning.
deadlineLabel: November 30, 2026 (recurring monthly-style cycle; winner announced December 1, 2026)

name: ScholarshipOwl No Essay Scholarship
description: For applicants over age 16 who are legal residents of the 50 U.S. states, D.C., or a U.S. territory (Rhode Island and Michigan residents excluded), enrolled or planning to enroll within three months of registering at a qualifying U.S. high school, college, or university. No essay required; four winners are randomly drawn each month.
deadlineLabel: Monthly drawing; no single fixed deadline — check sponsor for the current month's cutoff

name: Georgia HOPE Scholarship
amount: Pays a per-credit-hour tuition rate set annually by the state, varying by institution (roughly $105–$306 per credit hour for 2025-26; some schools use a flat per-term rate instead)
description: For U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens meeting Georgia residency rules (generally 12 consecutive months of residency for those who graduated Georgia high schools, 24 months for others) who are degree-seeking students in good academic standing at an eligible University System of Georgia, Technical College System of Georgia, or private HOPE-eligible Georgia college. Requires Selective Service registration where applicable, compliance with the Georgia Drug-Free Postsecondary Education Act, and no default on prior federal or Georgia financial aid.
deadlineLabel: No single deadline — applications are accepted through the last day of the school term or a student's withdrawal date, whichever comes first; apply early since individual colleges may set their own earlier deadlines

name: New York Excelsior Scholarship Program
amount: Last-dollar award covering tuition at a SUNY or CUNY college after other aid (e.g., Pell, TAP) is applied, for 2–5 years depending on the degree program
description: For U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens with 12 continuous months of New York State residency, household combined federal adjusted gross income of $125,000 or less, pursuing an undergraduate degree full-time (12+ credits/term, 30+ credits/year) at a SUNY or CUNY college. Non-residents, including undocumented students, apply through the NYS DREAM Act instead. Recipients who move out of New York after graduating must repay the award as a loan, and award years used count against a service/residency requirement to live and work in New York after graduation.
deadlineLabel: The NYS Excelsior Scholarship program is now closed for the 2026-27 academic year — check hesc.ny.gov for the next application window

name: Tennessee Promise
amount: Last-dollar scholarship covering tuition and mandatory fees not covered by the Pell Grant, HOPE Scholarship, or Tennessee Student Assistance Award at Tennessee's community colleges, Colleges of Applied Technology, or eligible four-year institutions offering an associate degree
description: For Tennessee high school seniors (class of 2027) who complete the TN Promise application, attend a mandatory meeting coordinated by their partnering mentoring organization (the Ayers Foundation Trust or tnAchieves, depending on county), submit the 2027-28 FAFSA by April 1, 2027, enroll full-time starting spring 2027, and complete 16 hours of community service (first 16 hours due August 1, 2027).

name: California Cal Grant Community College Entitlement Award
amount: Varies by financial need and school costs; covers tuition/fee gaps at California Community Colleges — exact award amounts are not published on the program page, contact CSAC for current figures
description: For students enrolling at a California Community College who submit a FAFSA (or CA Dream Act Application) along with a verified Cal Grant GPA, and who meet the California Student Aid Commission's general income, asset, and residency eligibility standards. A related Cal Grant C award (no GPA requirement) is available for students in occupational or technical programs who meet the same financial standards.
deadlineLabel: September 2 for the Community College Entitlement Award (date may shift slightly year to year) — confirm the current cycle's exact date with the California Student Aid Commission
